correctness.rationale: Euclid bijection and exact polynomial F are correct. Dyadic odd-factor difference proves a permutation on even residues; ternary gradient is nonzero at every admissible base class, yielding 8·3^(e-1) lifts. CRT gives 16Q exact fibers mod 6Q. Mobius over d coprime six and a sector lattice estimate gives X/(2πQ)+O_Q(√X log(2X)); p≥5 zero-fiber has 4(p−1) points among p²−1. The packaged finite checker verifies 41 test families without replacing the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Exact all-depth local equidistribution of normalized primitive Pythagorean areas modulo 2^a3^b, and the classification of precisely these uniform moduli, are not supplied by the inspected Euclid-parameter, area-divisibility, aggregate-counting or thin-orbit sieve results. The odd-prime four-line obstruction is partially anticipated in Kontorovich–Oh and is not by itself advanced as novel.
residual_risks: The 2-adic/3-adic fiber law might be an unindexed implicit corollary in the literature on local densities for primitive polynomial orbits; the searches cannot exclude this.
The four-line odd-prime obstruction is already broadly reflected in Kontorovich–Oh and should not be treated as an independently novel component.
The fixed-modulus error follows a standard primitive lattice-count argument and is not a proposed improvement over known general lattice-point estimates.

value.rationale: The maximal set of equidistribution moduli for the normalized area of primitive integer right triangles is a natural, complete arithmetic classification. The all-level exact local fiber uniformity at 2 and 3, effective global counting consequence and explicit nonuniform prime obstruction explain the phenomenon structurally, well beyond a finite tabulation or compulsory divisibility by six.
